title: 新游汇总：Monster Hunter、Saints Row、No Man’s Sky、Digimon、Darkest Dungeon、Cut The Rope 等
content:
New game digest: Monster Hunter, Saints Row, No Man’s Sky, Digimon, Darkest Dungeon, Cut The Rope, more – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content

Monster Hunter Outlanders (TiMi Studio Group)
Tencent-owned TiMi Studio Group
launched Monster Hunter Outlanders
on iOS and Android on October 29, almost two years after it was announced. The free-to-play survival hunting action game is developed under licence from Capcom. A mainland China version is planned for 2027 or later.
Saints Row: The Third Remastered (Feral Interactive)
Feral Interactive’s port of
Saints Row: The Third Remastered
is out now on iOS and Android, priced at $19.99, £12.99 and €15.99. The open-world action game includes all DLC and online co-op, with gamepad support on all devices and keyboard and mouse support on iPad and Android.
No Man’s Sky (Hello Games)
Hello Games released
No Man’s Sky
on iPhone and iPad on October 28. The space exploration survival game is free to try, with a one-time $19.99 unlock for the full game, and needs an iPhone 11 or newer.
Multiplayer and planetary settlements are the only major features missing from the iOS version. There is no word on an Android release.
Digimon Alysion (Bandai)
Bandai has opened
pre-registration for Digimon Alysion
on iOS and Android in 49 countries and regions. The free-to-play digital card game adapts the physical Digimon Card Game and features an original story set in the world of the Digimon Liberator webcomic and light novel.
A 10,000-player closed beta ran in August 2025. Bandai is aiming for a 2026 release but has not set a date.
Darkest Dungeon II (Playdigious)
Playdigious is bringing Red Hook Studios’ Darkest Dungeon II to iOS and Android in 2027. The mobile version of the gothic roguelike, built around turn-based battles, was revealed at The Mobile Premiere on October 28.
Cut the Rope Remastered (ZeptoLab)
ZeptoLab’s
Cut the Rope Remastered
launches on iOS and Android on December 3 as a premium game with no ads, in-app purchases or subscriptions. Pre-registering players get a launch discount.
The physics puzzler was previously an Apple Arcade exclusive, developed with Paladin Studios.
One Piece: Grand Gourmet (Bandai Namco)
Bandai Namco and Kairosoft released
One Piece: Grand Gourmet
on October 23 for iOS, Android, Switch, Switch 2 and PC via Steam.
The pixel-art management sim lets players run a restaurant ship with the Straw Hat Crew, with more than 400 characters from the series appearing as staff and customers.
Neural Dawn (Arm)
Arm and Sumo Digital’s
Neural Dawn
is now available on Android devices powered by Arm’s Mali G2-Ultra NX GPU. The third-person adventure showcases Arm’s AI-based neural graphics tech and is the first mobile game to use Unreal Engine’s MegaLights lighting system.
Arm says a team of 17 at Sumo built it in 18 months.
He is Coming (Playdigious)
Roguelite autobattler RPG He is Coming is heading to iOS and Android in 2027. Playdigious is reworking it for mobile with original developer Chronocle.
Players combine gear to take on the Demon King’s minions or other players in a separate mode.
Everything is Crab (Secret Mode)
Animal evolution roguelite Everything is Crab launches on iOS and Android on November 24, with a reworked touchscreen control scheme and the same content as the PC version. Console editions follow on January 26, 2027.
It is the debut game from Malmö studio Odd Dreams Digital. Secret Mode says it has sold more than 650,000 copies on PC since its May launch.
Vampire Therapist (Little Bat Games)
BAFTA-nominated visual novel
Vampire Therapist
arrives on iOS and Android on November 24. The free download covers the tutorial and first two therapy sessions, and the full game includes all free updates and the Couples Therapy DLC.
Berlin studio Little Bat Games first released it on PC in 2024. Android pre-registration is open now.
Astro Burn (Pixel Doors)
Pixel Doors and developer Beyond The Pixels have released Astro Burn worldwide on iPhone and iPad, following its PC and Android launches. The 90s-style cute ’em up arcade shooter stars a space cat called Astro.
Pines Peak: Merge Travel Games (Vizor)
Flexion has
launched Vizor’s Pines Peak
on “alternative app stores” including Amazon Appstore, Samsung Galaxy Store, Huawei AppGallery, Xiaomi GetApps and One store. Glera Games developed the casual merge game.
It is the third Vizor title Flexion has taken to alternative app stores, after Klondike Adventures and Mahjong Treasure Quest.
Ludo Go – Dice Board Games (Easybrain)
Easybrain’s hypercasual board game
Ludo Go
arrived on the UK App Store on October 20, according to AppMagic, following an earlier Android release. The level-based take on Ludo adds special pieces such as the Joker.
AppMagic estimates just over 900,000 downloads across both versions, with India as its biggest market.
Color Away – Tap Block Puzzle (Easybrain)
Easybrain has also released Color Away on Google Play in the US, with AppMagic listing an October 21 release date. In the puzzle game, players tap coloured blocks to send them through walls of the same colour, working out the right order to clear the board. Right now, the game appears to have been soft launched in India, Puerto Rico, and the US.
